content: 1. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of ritonavir by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters and hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered, and close monitoring is recommended. 2. Rifampin decreases the levels of rivaroxaban by enhancing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and dose adjustments may be necessary if co-administration is unavoidable. 3. Rifampin significantly reduces the levels of roflumilast by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP1A2 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may reduce therapeutic efficacy. 4. Rifampin decreases the efficacy of rolapitant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Long-term co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided, and alternative therapies are recommended. 5. Rifampin reduces the levels of romidepsin by inducing P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. 6. Rifampin decreases the levels of ropinirole by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 7. Rifampin increases the toxicity of rosuvastatin by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Close monitoring is required. 8. Rifampin reduces the levels of ruxolitinib (both systemic and topical) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 9. Rifampin increases the levels of sacubitril/valsartan by affecting hepatic uptake transporters (OATP1B1). 10. Sarecycline increases rifampin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein. Toxicities should be monitored, and dosage adjustments may be required. 11. Rifampin reduces the levels of saxagliptin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 12. Rifampin decreases the levels of seladelpar by increasing its metabolism. Biochemical responses (e.g., ALP and bilirubin) should be monitored during co-administration. 13. Rifampin reduces the levels of selegiline by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 14. Rifampin decreases the levels of selexipag by inducing CYP2C8, UGT1A3, and 2B7 enzymes. The selexipag dose may need to be doubled if co-administered with rifampin. 15. Rifampin reduces the levels of selpercatinib and selumetinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 16. Rifampin decreases sildenafil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Potent CYP3A4 inducers can significantly reduce sildenafil plasma levels, requiring close monitoring. 17. Rifampin reduces the levels of silodosin by inducing P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 18. Rifampin increases simvastatin toxicity by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters, increasing the risk of myopathy. Close monitoring is required. 19. Rifampin reduces the levels of siponimod by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended. 20. Rifampin decreases the levels of sirolimus by inducing P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 21. Sodium bicarbonate reduces rifampin absorption when co-administered. Rifampin should be taken at least one hour before antacids. 22. Rifampin reduces the efficacy of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. 23. Rifampin increases the toxicity of magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride by causing fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, which may lead to seizures, arrhythmias, or renal impairment. Close monitoring is required. 24. Rifampin reduces the levels of sofosbuvir and sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by inducing P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it may reduce antiviral efficacy. 25. Rifampin decreases the levels of solifenacin and sonidegib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 26. Rifampin reduces the levels of sorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 27. Rifampin decreases sotagliflozin levels by inducing UGT1A9 metabolism, potentially reducing its efficacy. Alternative drugs should be used. 28. Rifampin reduces the levels of sotorasib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. 29. Rifampin decreases the levels of sparsentan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 30. Rifampin reduces the levels of stiripentol by inducing CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2C19 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 31. Rifampin decreases the levels of streptomycin and sufentanil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 32. Rifampin reduces the levels of sulbactam/durlobactam by inhibiting OATP1 transporters. Alternative drugs should be used. 33. Rifampin decreases the levels of sulfamethoxazole by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but close monitoring is advised. 34. Rifampin reduces the levels of sunitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 35. Rifampin decreases the levels of suvorexant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If a higher dose is required, it should not exceed 20 mg/day. 36. Rifampin reduces the levels of tacrolimus by inducing P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 37. Rifampin decreases tadalafil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, especially in pulmonary hypertension patients. 38. Rifampin reduces tamoxifen levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 39. Rifampin decreases tamsulosin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 40. Rifampin reduces tasimelteon levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. 41. Rifampin decreases tazemetostat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 42. Rifampin reduces temsirolimus levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 43. Rifampin decreases teniposide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 44. Rifampin reduces tramadol levels and its active metabolite by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 metabolism. Close monitoring is necessary. 45. Rifampin decreases trazodone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 46. Rifampin reduces triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 47. Rifampin decreases triazolam levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 48. Rifampin reduces trimethoprim levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required. 49. Rifampin decreases trimipramine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is necessary. 50. Rifampin reduces typhoid vaccine live efficacy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 51. Rifampin decreases ubrogepant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 52. Rifampin reduces ulipristal levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 53. Rifampin decreases upadacitinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. 54. Rifampin increases valsartan levels by inhibiting OATP1B1 transporters. Close monitoring is required. 55. Rifampin reduces vandetanib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 56. Rifampin decreases vardenafil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 57. Rifampin reduces vemurafenib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 58. Rifampin decreases venetoclax levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided. 59. Rifampin reduces verapamil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used. 60. Rifampin decreases vilazodone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments may be necessary. 61. Rifampin reduces vinblastine levels by inducing P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be used.
